4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Nia Morgna and Lileas Graf scheduled a meeting to discuss an ongoing legal case that required my attention.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Early in the morning, we convened in my office.

6.speaker: Lileas Graf
6.text: "Thank you for being here at this hour, Mr. President."

7.speaker: Nia Morgna
7.text: "There is a court case initiated by a Bludish citizen which involves a possible revision of the constitution. Unfortunately, it has the potential to affect the whole country."

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Nia stacked the papers in front of her.
8.conditionsRaw:
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true

12.speaker: Lileas Graf
12.text: "We need to inform you about some news from Bergia."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "Great. Bad news from Bergia again. What's new?"

16.speaker: Lileas Graf
16.text: "I'll start from the beginning. As you know, after the discovery of KA-74s in separatist hideouts, there have been more than a few attacks initiated and claimed by the BFF."

17.speaker: Lileas Graf
17.text: "However, with the rising tensions after Operation Bear Trap, we have also been receiving more and more intelligence about some kind of a 'preparation' by the terrorists."

18.speaker: Lileas Graf
18.text: "Due to the decrease of security funds, many of these -- otherwise avoidable -- attacks couldn't be stopped. This created some hysteria inside Bergia."

22.speaker: Lileas Graf
22.text: "Thanks to the increase in security funding, many of these attacks were stopped before they were executed."

23.speaker: Lileas Graf
23.text: "Due to the lack of security funding, some of these -- otherwise avoidable -- attacks couldn't be stopped. This led to some increase in the tensions in Bergia."

27.speaker: Nia Morgna
27.text: "Unfortunately, the court backlog is piling up with increasingly frequent rulings that are unjust. This has led to many of our citizens losing their trust in our justice system. This is particularly a problem for the residents of Bergia."

28.speaker: Lileas Graf
28.text: "It increased even further after Operation Bear Trap. We have been receiving more and more intelligence about some kind of a 'preparation' by the terrorists."

29.speaker: Nia Morgna
29.text: "It's definitely not helping with the increasing tensions between the Bludish populace and Sords."

33.speaker: Lileas Graf
33.text: "We'll get there, Ms. Morgna. As I was saying..."

34.speaker: Nia Morgna
34.text: "I agree with you that the threat has been exaggerated. However, the court case that I'm looking ov-"

35.speaker: Lileas Graf
35.text: "The increasing threat of the BFF led Governor Bron to -- justifiably -- resort to his emergency powers to curb the danger."

36.speaker: Lileas Graf
36.text: "His discovery of militant training grounds disguised as schools was commendable, as well as his quick handling of bomb threats coming from major cities like Deyr."

37.speaker: Lileas Graf
37.text: "However, his latest policies have been questionable. Especially the 'Peaceful Resettlement' order. It has been met with massive anger from the majority of the Bluds in the region."

38.speaker: Player
38.conditionsRaw:
((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true) == false)

39.speaker: Nia Morgna
39.text: "Ishval Ersen is claiming that the current constitution gives the legal grounds to discriminate against Bludish people, directly infringing upon their rights as citizens."

40.speaker: Nia Morgna
40.text: "He claims Article 7 of the constitution -- citing the line: 'Every Sord is equal before the law' -- is in direct conflict with the freedoms and rights defined in Article 100."

41.speaker: Nia Morgna
41.text: "Governor Phelix Bron is accused of using Article 7 to justify his oppression of the Bludish community."

42.speaker: Player
42.text: "What are the accusations against the governor?"
42.conditionsRaw:
((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false)

43.speaker: Player
43.conditionsRaw:
((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true) == false)

44.speaker: Lileas Graf
44.text: "Mr. Bron has sadly evicted thousands of Bluds from their homes in Deyr recently. The fact that this happened in a city with relatively low levels of BFF activity is a sloppy decision at best."

45.speaker: Nia Morgna
45.text: "A sloppy decision? This is a direct violation of their right to property. The BFF activity levels have nothing to do with this."

46.speaker: Lileas Graf
46.text: "But it does, Ms. Morgna. The state can take any measures to fight with terror inside its borders. The decision would have been justified if those neighborhoods were in fact labelled as 'threat level red'."

47.speaker: Lileas Graf
47.text: "...But they were not. Hence, he did not have the authority to evict those citizens. In this case in Deyr, the governor has definitely violated his authority."

48.speaker: Nia Morgna
48.text: "There are hundreds of accusations listed in this case, ranging from violent actions by law enforcement officers to open discrimination in local municipalities."

49.speaker: Nia Morgna
49.text: "You are underplaying it. This eviction was only the last of the many he ordered as part of Bergia's *peaceful resettlement policies*. This is not about Deyr."

50.speaker: Nia Morgna
50.text: "Ishval Ersen is a lawyer and Bludish rights activist. He lives in Deyr and has experienced the systemic racism in the region firsthand."

51.speaker: Nia Morgna
51.text: "He was evicted last month from his home in Deyr on the grounds of 'threatening public stability and safety'."

52.speaker: Nia Morgna
52.text: "He was also shot at by local law enforcement forces several times in the last two years and managed to survive it all so far. The attackers, of course, were never punished."

53.speaker: Lileas Graf
53.text: "As much as the eviction seems unjust, Mr. Ersen must be further investigated for his potential ties to dangerous organizations. I'd like to believe the forces wouldn't have fired at him without proper reason."

54.speaker: Player
54.text: "What exactly does Ersen claim about the conflict in the constitution?"
54.conditionsRaw:
((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option1"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option3"] == true  and 
Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option4"] == true) == false)

55.speaker: Nia Morgna
55.text: "As you know, the rights and liberties Article 7 alludes to are described in Article 100 in further detail."

56.speaker: Nia Morgna
56.text: "Mr. Ersen claims the line: 'Every Sord is equal before the law' in Article 7 does not include other ethnicities and thus gives the state the right to suspend or limit the rights of non-Sords defined in Article 100."

57.speaker: Nia Morgna
57.text: "All citizens, in theory, can exercise their rights described in these articles and are equally subject to law as described, and these rights cannot be suspended by the government under any circumstances other than a defensive war."

58.speaker: Nia Morgna
58.text: "Courts have repeatedly protected Governor Bron in the past, and it is true that he bets on Mr. Hawker justifying his actions through Article 7. However, there is also Article 6 -- which the courts could have taken into account already."

59.speaker: Player
59.text: "And what is the problem with Article 6?"

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "Article 7 is an embarrassment that needs to be removed. I wish we could also tackle this in our proposal for constitutional change."

62.speaker: Nia Morgna
62.text: "I'm not sure how you'd manage that at this stage of the process."

63.speaker: Nia Morgna
63.text: "As you know, Article 6 goes: 'Everyone who is bound to the Sordish state by citizenship is a Sord'."

64.speaker: Nia Morgna
64.text: "But did you ask Bludish people what they think? Yes, it's true that this article has protected them on a number of occasions, as it defines Sord as a non-ethnic term, but it is left up to the interpretation of the courts."

65.speaker: Lileas Graf
65.text: "Which clarifies clearly that the constitution does not discriminate against other ethnicities or cultures. Citizens of this country are called Sords."

66.speaker: Nia Morgna
66.text: "They could have argued that Article 6 extends the rights defined in Article 7 to all citizens of Sordland regardless of race. But they didn't. Yet."

69.speaker: Nia Morgna
69.text: "That is a massive understatement. Governor Bron has abused his powers and clearly acted against the constitution."

70.speaker: Nia Morgna
70.text: "And quite surprisingly, Ishval Ersen has managed to successfully push his case to the higher courts. He is suing Phelix Bron for infringing upon the liberties of Bludish people."

71.speaker: Nia Morgna
71.text: "He also raises a conflict in the constitution and argues that the way it is written makes it open to interpretation and allows people like Governor Bron to abuse their powers."

75.speaker: Nia Morgna
75.text: "It wasn't a possibility according to the preliminary committee meetings."

76.speaker: Nia Morgna
76.text: "But there might be a way around it in the near future."

77.speaker: Nia Morgna
77.text: "They can potentially push this case to the Supreme Court."

86.speaker: Player
86.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["BaseGameIsolated.BergiaProblemMeeting_Hub_Option2"] == true  and

91.speaker: Nia Morgna
91.text: "In any case... The situation might be troubling if it reaches the Supreme Court and Mr. Hawker manages to sabotage it by altering the current interpretation. It would be disastrous for Bludish rights."

92.speaker: Nia Morgna
92.text: "I will be doing my best to ensure a positive result comes out of this case. But I'm not sure if the centrists would be willing to agree with Mr. Ersen."

93.speaker: Lileas Graf
93.text: "Why would Mr. Hawker even sabotage it? The current interpretation is strictly Sollist. I'm sure he will follow the constitution and charge Governor Bron for unconstitutional behavior."

94.speaker: Lileas Graf
94.text: "According to the foundational values of this republic, everyone who is a citizen of this country is a Sord. The constitution is clear about this and does not allow for discrimination."

95.speaker: Nia Morgna
95.text: "Maybe Hawker is not the man you think he is, Ms. Graf. From what I've heard, his stance on this subject may not be the standard Sollist interpretation but... something darker."

96.speaker: Nia Morgna
96.text: "I'm afraid he'll reject the case altogether and find Governor Bron innocent. If this happens, it would make discrimination against Bludish people legal."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Do you think Justice Hawker and the Old Guards would go that far?"

98.speaker: Player
98.text: "What if we can convince the Justices to agree with Ersen? Wouldn't that give us precedent to change said articles of the constitution?"

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "This is insane. Isn't there anything I can do?"

100.speaker: Nia Morgna
100.text: "According to the rumors within the Supreme Court, yes. It is already unusual that the case is making its way up to them."

101.speaker: Nia Morgna
101.text: "If the Supreme Court agrees that the constitution is in conflict with itself, yes... But I don't know if you are serious or not, Mr. President."

102.speaker: Nia Morgna
102.text: "I'm afraid not, Mr. President. The executive has no jurisdiction over the judiciary."

103.speaker: Player
103.text: "You must put pressure on the system and block this case from reaching the Supreme Court, Ms. Morgna."

104.speaker: Nia Morgna
104.text: "I'm afraid even Justice Edmonds and the centrists would be completely against that. It would be a very difficult scenario."

105.speaker: Nia Morgna
105.text: "And in this case, I'm afraid even Justice Edmonds and the centrists would be almost impossible to convince."

106.speaker: Nia Morgna
106.text: "Of course. I will do my best, Mr. President."

107.speaker: Lileas Graf
107.text: "To be honest, I don't think this is a matter for our administration. We must keep out from judicial affairs."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "Honestly, I couldn't care less. It would be better for this country."

110.speaker: Nia Morgna
110.text: "I hope you are joking, Mr. President."

111.speaker: Player
111.text: "What the Bludish community is going through in Bergia is unacceptable. We must do what it takes to stop this madness."

112.speaker: Player
112.text: "Ms. Graf is right. We must first be completely sure that Mr. Ersen is innocent."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "Are you joking, Ms. Graf? You'd like to *believe*? The police are getting out of control under your management."

114.speaker: Lileas Graf
114.text: "What's that supposed to mean? I'm not even in control of the forces that are being blamed here. Governor Bron has his own security forces."

116.speaker: Lileas Graf
116.text: "I will look into it, Mr. President."

117.speaker: Lileas Graf
117.text: "My forces were not involved in any of this. It was Bergian police. Bergia's special zone is what allowed this to happen in the first place."

118.speaker: Nia Morgna
118.text: "As much as I hate to say it, I somewhat agree with Lileas on this. I'd prefer to keep the status quo over risking a complete abolishment of rights. We still have the power to make tangible reforms."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "Your lack of faith is disappointing. I must say I didn't expect that from you. And what about your tangible reforms?"

120.speaker: Nia Morgna
120.text: "I'm simply stating the obvious, Mr. President. Instead of openly attacking the court, we can bring real change with our lawmaking powers."

121.speaker: Lileas Graf
121.text: "As I said, I think the government has better things to do than meddle with judicial affairs."

122.speaker: Lileas Graf
122.text: "There is, however, something that the government can do to address the situation on the ground."

123.speaker: Lileas Graf
123.text: "It is time we push for change within the security structure of Bergia and the special status that resulted in de facto autonomy. It clearly isn't working."

124.speaker: Nia Morgna
124.text: "The resettlement policies in Bergia and the Ersen case have changed the mood of the lawmakers. We can use this opportunity to push for the removal of Tarquin Soll's security zone decree. It is a much bigger possibility than before."

125.speaker: Lileas Graf
125.text: "Ms. Morgna is right. There is something that the government can do to address the situation on the ground."

126.speaker: Nia Morgna
126.text: "Of course racism is rampant throughout our country, but Bludish citizens inside Bergia are having a much worse time than the Bludish residents of cities like Lachaven or Holsord. If we focus on Bergia, we can remove its special status."

127.speaker: Nia Morgna
127.text: "This alone would be a huge step for Bludish rights. Unfortunately, as long as Governor Bron is in charge of Bergia with the powers he has, no judicial reforms would reverse the situation on the ground."

128.speaker: Lileas Graf
128.text: "To put it simply, we want to work on a detailed proposal to restructure Bergia. I believe it must become a region of Sordland like any other. We must centralize the system and abolish the local security forces."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "Are you absolutely certain that your security forces can do a better job than Bergian police?"

130.speaker: Player
130.text: "I don't see how a local change is more important than removing the basis of discrimination in our very constitution."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "Are you sure we can even revoke the special status of Bergia?"

141.speaker: Player
141.text: "You are right. We shouldn't meddle in the judiciary."

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "I don't agree with changing the structure in Bergia now. We shouldn't disrupt Governor Bron's policies."

143.speaker: Nia Morgna
143.text: "We can't be sure of anything, Mr. President. You know this better than me."

144.speaker: Lileas Graf
144.text: "It is true. Some members of my circle inside the party are keen on this as well. They are starting to believe Soll's policy in Bergia has already run its course."

145.speaker: Nia Morgna
145.text: "But Lileas and I both believe there is potential to get more MPs behind the idea."

146.speaker: Lileas Graf
146.text: "It is discouraging to hear this from you, Mr. President. My team and our officers on the ground are comprised of the most well-trained and patriotic individuals."

147.speaker: Lileas Graf
147.text: "With Bergia under complete control of the central administration, we will no longer hear about reports of injustice against our Bludish citizens."

148.speaker: Lileas Graf
148.text: "We can't allow the conflict in Wehlen to spread to Sordland. And we know that the Wehlen and Sordland divisions of the BFF are in close cooperation."

149.speaker: Nia Morgna
149.text: "Well, Mr. President, if your insane proposal somehow makes it, your new powers would allow you to enact this by decree anyway."

150.speaker: Nia Morgna
150.text: "If we play our cards right during the process of this case while we work on the preparation of a strong proposal for the special zone, we can gather enough support behind it."
150.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Weaker"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Weaker"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Removed"] == true)

151.speaker: Nia Morgna
151.text: "Well, Mr. President, with a strong enough proposal and some judicial support, your current powers might be just enough to be able to enact this by decree as well."
151.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Weaker"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Removed"] == true) == false)

153.speaker: Nia Morgna
153.text: "In any case, I think it is also possible to get this through the Assembly."

157.speaker: Player
157.text: "Why stop with Bergia? We have to eventually change Articles 6 and 7 as well."

158.speaker: Lileas Graf
158.text: "Nia and I both agree that we need to abolish the Special Zone of Bergia. This is the first point that the proposal will address."

159.speaker: Player
159.text: "I think this might be too risky to push at the same time with our constitutional amendments."

160.speaker: Nia Morgna
160.text: "I'm glad that we agree. Of course we should push for that in our next amendments."

161.speaker: Nia Morgna
161.text: "It's not. But when the forces on the ground don't even respect the constitution, fixing it alone would not suffice."

162.speaker: Lileas Graf
162.text: "Let's wake up to the real world. There is no way the Assembly or the Court would pass an amendment to Article 6 or 7."

163.speaker: Nia Morgna
163.text: "If our current proposal passes, we will no longer need the Court to change the constitution."

167.speaker: Nia Morgna
167.text: "And the Assembly can always be convinced later."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "I still think we can add these amendments to our proposal before the vote. The current proposal can still be modified."

170.speaker: Lileas Graf
170.text: "You can do whatever you want with your amendments, Mr. President. But at least hear about our proposal first."

171.speaker: Nia Morgna
171.text: "I'm not going to deny the risk but we can no longer look away."

172.speaker: Lileas Graf
172.text: "Before we get distracted, I'd like to briefly talk about the details of the proposal."

173.speaker: Nia Morgna
173.text: "I can't believe it. Are you really supportive of Governor Bron's policies, Mr. President?"

174.speaker: Lileas Graf
174.text: "On the other hand, the community police have been very helpful in the areas where they were allowed to serve -- which aren't many, unfortunately."

178.speaker: Lileas Graf
178.text: "The main problem is with the security structure of Bergia. Due to the special status of the region, operations on the ground are run by local security forces that are not bound to the Interior."

183.speaker: Player
183.text: "That's precisely why we joined the operation. To destroy the BFF once and for all."

187.speaker: Player
187.text: "That's precisely why we're cooperating with Wehzek forces to defend our borders."

188.speaker: Nia Morgna
188.text: "The main problem is not security but the very right to existence of the Bludish people. I'd still like to believe your perspective can be changed on this subject."

189.speaker: Lileas Graf
189.text: "This would also mean taking away the special authority of the governor."

190.speaker: Nia Morgna
190.text: "I agree with removing the governor as well as his insane authority. But I don't support a complete centralization of the region. I propose that we restructure the Special Zone, democratize it and acknowledge the Bludish movement."

191.speaker: Lileas Graf
191.text: "How does that resolve anything? How do you solve any problem by dividing the region from the rest of Sordland? We've tried that already."

192.speaker: Lileas Graf
192.text: "My proposal is very simple. The special zone must be fully revoked, governor's powers taken away and the local security forces must be abolished. Only then Bergia can be an equal part of Sordland."

193.speaker: Lileas Graf
193.text: "We will hold local municipal elections just like every city in Sordland, and the security of the region will be under the full control of the Ministry of the Interior. We can no longer allow their forces to pursue violence with impunity."

194.speaker: Nia Morgna
194.text: "If this was a problem that the central government could fix, your mighty Colonel would have solved it already. The assimilation policies clearly didn't work."

195.speaker: Nia Morgna
195.text: "Millions of Bludish people suffered over the last decades. We saw a massive uprising, terror attacks and a governor going rogue. These people only wanted to live in this country as equals, but they were denied that."

196.speaker: Nia Morgna
196.text: "Why don't we allow Bergians to elect their own local government? Why is Holsord so keen on prying into the lives of the Bludish people?"

197.speaker: Lileas Graf
197.text: "I'm sorry to tell you, Ms. Morgna, but Bergia is part of Sordland as much as Agnland or Holsord. You're bringing secessionist Fetih Ejall's lifelong quest here as *your proposal*. What's wrong with you?"

198.speaker: Lileas Graf
198.text: "What's next? Secession of Bergia and a formation of an independent Bludish state? Autonomy for Agnland? And why don't you hold a referendum for the Rums of Estord, and ask them if they want to join Rumburg while you're at it?"

199.speaker: Player
199.text: "Lileas has a point. Bergia shouldn't have any restrictions or privileges compared to any other region."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "Hold on, Lileas. I want to hear Nia's proposal."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "I agree with Lileas. Replacing a special zone with another one wouldn't help anyone."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "I don't agree with either of your points."

203.speaker: Lileas Graf
203.text: "I will provide you with a more detailed report later about the damage Governor Bron has done for Blud-Sord relations as well as security. You would surely agree with me."

205.speaker: Nia Morgna
205.text: "We should replace the oppressive laws of the special zone with a democratic system that allows for proper local representation. I propose the 'Bergia Semi-Autonomous Region'."

206.speaker: Lileas Graf
206.text: "I propose we unite Bergia with the rest of Sordland and enforce the same laws and policies as any other Sordish region -- dismantling the current semi-independent security structure in the process."

207.speaker: Nia Morgna
207.text: "I'm just saying the solution is not a rushed 'unification'. We must acknowledge that Bergia is a unique region with its own culture and history. We cannot disregard the social reality."

210.speaker: Player
210.text: "I'm supportive of a semi-autonomous Bergia. This is what the mainstream Bludish movement wants."

211.speaker: Player
211.text: "I also want to hear Ms. Graf's proposal before deciding."

215.speaker: Player
215.text: "I don't agree with either of you. I'd rather not risk any drastic change like that. Bergia should stay as it is."

216.speaker: Player
216.text: "Both proposals fail to impress me. I want to start working on the possibility of adding new amendments to our proposal instead, so we can get to the root of the matter."

220.speaker: Player
220.text: "Nia has a point. Peaceful assimilation is also not the solution. We must finally listen to what the Bludish people want."

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "I'm supportive of Lileas' plan to revoke the special status of Bergia and unify it with the rest of Sordland."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "I also want to hear Ms. Morgna's proposal before deciding."

223.speaker: Player
223.text: "I don't agree with either of you. I'd rather not risk any drastic change like that. Bergia should stay as it is."

224.speaker: Player
224.text: "Both proposals fail to impress me. I want to start working on the possibility of adding new amendments to our proposal. Our proposal should expand the rights to everyone."

227.speaker: Nia Morgna
227.text: "How serious are you really, Mr. President?"

231.speaker: Lileas Graf
231.text: "I completely disagree. Please hear me out, Mr. President."

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: They both gave me a puzzled look.

240.speaker: Lileas Graf
240.text: "So it's decided, then? I can start working on the proposal as soon as possible?"

241.speaker: Nia Morgna
241.text: "Great. I can start working on the proposal immediately."

242.speaker: Nia Morgna
242.text: "Are you serious, Mr. President? Are we really going to ignore this massive problem?"

243.speaker: Lileas Graf
243.text: "As much as I believed in the Special Zone when it was first initiated by Colonel Soll, the times are changing, Mr. President. And I'm saying this as a proud Sollist."

244.speaker: Player
244.text: "Yes. It's been decided, Ms. Graf. You can get to work immediately. I'm counting on you."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "On second thought, semi-autonomy is the way to go. Start the work immediately, Ms. Morgna. I'm counting on you."

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "On second thought... I think it's best if we keep the status quo. We will not change anything about Bergia."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "Yes. It's been decided, Ms. Morgna. You can get to work immediately. I'm counting on you."

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "On a second thought, centralization is the way to go. Start the work immediately, Ms. Graf. I'm counting on you."

249.speaker: Player
249.text: "On a second thought... I think it's best if we keep the status quo. We will not change anything about Bergia."

250.speaker: Player
250.text: "I believe I was very clear. We will keep the status quo and not change anything about Bergia."

251.speaker: Player
251.text: "On second thought, semi-autonomy is the way to go. Start the work immediately, Ms. Morgna. I'm counting on you."

252.speaker: Player
252.text: "On second thought, centralization is the way to go. Start the work immediately, Ms. Graf. I'm counting on you."

254.speaker: Nia Morgna
254.text: "Thank you, Mr. President. I'll start working on it immediately."

255.speaker: Lileas Graf
255.text: "I must say I'm disappointed, Mr. President."

256.speaker: Nia Morgna
256.text: "With your constitutional proposal on the horizon, I expected a different response."

260.speaker: Nia Morgna
260.text: "I share the same sentiments as Lileas on this, Mr. President. Your inaction is frankly very disappointing."

261.speaker: Nia Morgna
261.text: "I shouldn't have expected anything from you. Especially right before your meeting with the National Front Party leadership to beg for votes."

262.speaker: Nia Morgna
262.text: "I share the same sentiments as Lileas on this, Mr. President. Your inaction is frankly very disappointing -- but of course, not very unexpected."

264.speaker: Narrator
264.text: Lileas looked incredibly furious, but kept herself quiet. I doubted that she would forget about this.

265.speaker: Lileas Graf
265.text: "Please, Ms. Morgna. You've heard the president."

266.speaker: Lileas Graf
266.text: "I will start working on the proposal immediately. It is very important to get this right, so it will take some time."

267.speaker: Lileas Graf
267.text: "My estimate is that it will be ready sometime after the vote on your constitutional amendments. You can choose to enact it then."

268.speaker: Nia Morgna
268.text: "To have a structure that will actually solve the problems of the region, we will need to conduct indepth research beforehand. I believe it will take some time."

269.speaker: Nia Morgna
269.text: "My estimate is that the proposal will be ready sometime after your constitutional amendments are voted on. You can choose whether to enact it then."

273.speaker: Nia Morgna
273.text: "You know that a change in your proposal at the last minute will lose you a lot of votes."

274.speaker: Nia Morgna
274.text: "Do you really think the USP will just accept it if you change the proposal that you've been promoting for so long?"

275.speaker: Nia Morgna
275.text: "I know that you have a meeting with the National Front Party's leader soon. And the reason is they are the only ones left who are willing to support you."

276.speaker: Nia Morgna
276.text: "Do you really want me to believe that you care about Bludish rights *that* much? And even if you did, I will not play into your hands and help a neo-Sollist alliance play populism."

277.speaker: Player
277.text: "Yes. I believe we can do it. I'm surprised you don't think the same."

278.speaker: Player
278.text: "I know it's risky but we have to try. I thought I could count on you."

279.speaker: Player
279.text: "Stop questioning me for a second, Ms. Morgna. How about you? What do you think?"

280.speaker: Player
280.text: "You're throwing big words around without thinking, Ms. Morgna. Can't you see I'm asking you to help me with this?"

281.speaker: Player
281.text: "I told you this before. With the new constitution we can do much more for the country. Why are you blocking me at every turn?"

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "You're right on that, Mr. Morgna. I will talk to Mr. Kibener because I need his vote. It doesn't mean I share their ideology."

283.speaker: Nia Morgna
283.text: "I don't care what you say, Mr. President. I did not take part in your amendments since I learned your position, and I intend to keep it that way."

284.speaker: Nia Morgna
284.text: "Know that the committee you formed will never include them in the proposal either. You built this all yourself. You can't blame me for anything."

286.speaker: Nia Morgna
286.text: "If you're insistent on taking that path, I will give you my full support, Mr. President."

287.speaker: Nia Morgna
287.text: "From the very first day, our aim in the reform committee was preparing something that is both politically realistic and effective."

288.speaker: Nia Morgna
288.text: "I believe this path directly conflicts with that initial target. This would make the proposal seem *extremely* radical."

289.speaker: Nia Morgna
289.text: "However, I completely agree with these changes and would support you fully if you're willing to go that way."

290.speaker: Nia Morgna
290.text: "You must know that it will take some time to come up with a proper proposal. It may not give us time to discuss the changes, let alone campaign for them."

291.speaker: Lileas Graf
291.text: "I and the USP would also definitely not allow you to do that, Mr. President."

292.speaker: Lileas Graf
292.text: "I think it's time we leave, Nia. The President surely has some other plans on his own."

296.speaker: Player
296.text: "Sounds like a plan, Ms. Morgna. Start the process immediately. I'm counting on you."

297.speaker: Nia Morgna
297.text: "Here's what we can do. I can start working on the wording of the new changes, and in parallel, evaluate how realistic it is to add this to our current proposal. We can try to include the Bludish leaders in the conversation as well."

298.speaker: Nia Morgna
298.text: "We'll try to prepare everything in time for you to have a last look. If you don't think it would work, you can feel free to leave it out of the proposal."

299.speaker: Nia Morgna
299.text: "We may still have some time to prepare it in time for the vote. However, I can't say how the party will react."

300.speaker: Player
300.text: "On second thought, it is better if we spend that time on a proposal to change the special zone of Bergia."

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "Sounds good, Ms. Morgna. I'm counting on you."

303.speaker: Player
303.text: "Sounds good, Ms. Graf. I'm counting on you."

305.speaker: Lileas Graf
305.text: "Don't waste your breath, Nia. The president has already made his decision."

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: They bid their farewells and left the room.

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: They bid their farewells and left the room.

318.speaker: Nia Morgna
318.text: "Of course, Mr. President. I'll get to work right away. Talk to you later."

319.speaker: Lileas Graf
319.text: "Great. I'll get to work. See you later, Mr. President."

320.speaker: Nia Morgna
320.text: "Great. I'll get to work. See you later, Mr. President."

323.speaker: Lileas Graf
323.text: "But I know when I'm not needed. Have a nice day."

324.speaker: Player
324.text: "Yes. I believe that is the way to go. Get to work on this immediately, Ms. Morgna. I'm counting on you."

325.speaker: Player
325.text: "No. Centralization is the way to go. Get to work on this immediately, Ms. Graf. I'm counting on you."

326.speaker: Nia Morgna
326.text: "Okay... So you want me to work on the proposal for the semi-autonomous special zone?"

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "Yes. I think he's doing a good job."

330.speaker: Player
330.text: "No. But I don't want my administration be involved with such a politically charged issue."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "I don't want to move against a USP figure right before our constitutional amendments are discussed."

332.speaker: Nia Morgna
332.text: "I understand your concerns but the atmosphere in the Assembly is changing, Mr. President. If we navigate this properly, this can be done."

333.speaker: Lileas Graf
333.text: "The reality is that we need to address the security problems in Bergia. This *Bludish issue* could get out of hand and become our number one national security threat."

334.speaker: Lileas Graf
334.text: "I thought the same once, Mr. President. But it's clearly not working. Bludish people are increasingly being radicalized and the BFF is exploiting the tensions the governor is creating."

335.speaker: Lileas Graf
335.text: "I would have agreed with you a couple of years ago, Mr. President. But the policies of the governor are clearly not working."

340.speaker: Lileas Graf
340.text: "I believe we are aligned on this matter, Mr. President."

341.speaker: Nia Morgna
341.text: "Mr. President. You asked me to explore options regarding the revocation of the Special Zone at the beginning of our term."

342.speaker: Nia Morgna
342.text: "Given the current circumstances, I think it is now possible."

343.speaker: Player
343.text: "Actually... I might have changed my mind since then."

344.speaker: Player
344.text: "That's great to hear. Tell me the details."

347.speaker: Nia Morgna
347.text: "Mr. President. This is very important. Please hear us out."

348.speaker: Player
348.text: "That's not the point. There is a reason why Bergia is a Special Zone. We cannot simply act like the secessionist movement doesn't exist."

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "That's precisely why I didn't make a deal with Wehlen."

353.speaker: Lileas Graf
353.text: "Well, it didn't seem to have stopped the tensions from increasing. Their war against the BFF has bolstered their resolve inside our country."

354.speaker: Lileas Graf
354.text: "Calm down, Nia dear. I'm not disagreeing with you."

355.speaker: Lileas Graf
355.text: "What does that have to do with anything?"

356.speaker: Narrator
356.text: Lileas Graf scheduled a meeting with me to discuss some important matters about the Special Zone of Bergia.

357.speaker: Narrator
357.text: She came to my office early in the morning.

358.speaker: Lileas Graf
358.text: "Thank you for being here at this hour, Mr. President."

359.speaker: Lileas Graf
359.text: "I need to inform you about some news from Bergia."

362.speaker: Player
362.text: "Great. Bad news from Bergia again. What's new?"

363.speaker: Lileas Graf
363.text: "I'll start from the beginning. As you know, after the discovery of KA-74s in separatist hideouts, there have been more than a few attacks initiated and claimed by the BFF."

368.speaker: Lileas Graf
368.text: "Due to the decrease in security funding, many of these -- otherwise avoidable -- attacks couldn't be stopped. This created some hysteria inside Bergia."

372.speaker: Lileas Graf
372.text: "Thanks to the emergency laws giving authority to our forces, many of these attacks were stopped before they could be executed."
372.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_IncreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_DecreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_AutocratEmergency_Extend"] == true)

373.speaker: Lileas Graf
373.text: "Thanks to the increase in security funding, many of these attacks were stopped before they could be executed."

374.speaker: Lileas Graf
374.text: "The main problem, however, lies with the security structure of Bergia. Due to the special status of the region, operations on the ground are run by local security forces that are not bound to the Interior."

379.speaker: Lileas Graf
379.text: "Due to the lack of security funding, some of these -- otherwise avoidable -- attacks couldn't be stopped. This led to some increase in the tensions in Bergia."
379.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_IncreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_DecreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_AutocratEmergency_Extend"] == true) == false)

384.speaker: Lileas Graf
384.text: "The threat of the BFF is growing larger, and we cannot respond efficiently if the Governor of the Special Zone doesn't cooperate with my forces."

385.speaker: Lileas Graf
385.text: "We cannot continue our fight against the targets of the emergency if the Governor of the Special Zone doesn't cooperate with my forces."

389.speaker: Lileas Graf
389.text: "I must also add... With the rising tensions after Operation Bear Trap, we have also been receiving more and more intelligence about some kind of a 'preparation' by the terrorists."

390.speaker: Lileas Graf
390.text: "We can't allow the conflict in Wehlen to spread to Sordland. And we know that both the Wehlen and Sordland divisions of the BFF are in close cooperation."

393.speaker: Player
393.text: "That's precisely why I didn't make a deal with Wehlen."

400.speaker: Player
400.text: "That's precisely why we joined the operation. To destroy the BFF once and for all."

401.speaker: Player
401.text: "That's precisely why we're cooperating with Wehzek forces to defend our borders."

405.speaker: Player
405.text: "I think this is overblown. The Bludish are not the targets of our emergency. I don't want to lose sight of our real targets."

406.speaker: Lileas Graf
406.text: "I must say that could have helped in this situation. Even though I myself was against the deal at the time."

407.speaker: Lileas Graf
407.text: "You're wrong, Mr. President. Even if the Bluds weren't your original targets, Governor Bron is using your emergency declaration as a justification to wage war against them."

411.speaker: Lileas Graf
411.text: "Maybe you were right about that decision, after all."

412.speaker: Lileas Graf
412.text: "Using your emergency declaration as a justification, Governor Bron is declaring war on the Bludish people with his powers as governor of the Special Zone."

413.speaker: Lileas Graf
413.text: "Feeling bolstered by the increasing threat of the BFF, Governor Bron is declaring war on the Bludish people with his powers as governor of the Special Zone."

417.speaker: Lileas Graf
417.text: "I know this is already what you wanted, Mr. President. But I don't think we can have Governor Bron in charge of the emergency there. He is going completely rogue."

418.speaker: Lileas Graf
418.text: "In short, he's ignored your original targets and gone completely rogue."

419.speaker: Lileas Graf
419.text: "I'm afraid he has gone rogue, Mr. President."

420.speaker: Lileas Graf
420.text: "But I believe it is time we push for change within the security structure of Bergia. Its special status resulted in de facto autonomy, which clearly isn't working."

421.speaker: Lileas Graf
421.text: "Unfortunately, he is under protection due to the absurd laws of the Special Zone. The Supreme Court doesn't want to move against him."

422.speaker: Player
422.text: "That's not the point. There is a reason why Bergia is a Special Zone. We cannot simply act like the secessionist movement doesn't exist."

423.speaker: Player
423.text: "Are you absolutely certain that your security forces can do a better job than Bergian police?"

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "How do we revoke the special status of Bergia?"

425.speaker: Player
425.text: "I don't agree with changing the structure in Bergia now. We shouldn't disrupt Governor Bron's policies."

426.speaker: Lileas Graf
426.text: "We can't be sure of anything, Mr. President. You know this better than me."

427.speaker: Lileas Graf
427.text: "Some of my circle inside the party are actually keen on this as well. They are starting to believe Soll's policy in Bergia has already run its course."

428.speaker: Lileas Graf
428.text: "But with the extreme actions of the governor, I believe there is a way to get more MPs behind the idea."

429.speaker: Lileas Graf
429.text: "It is discouraging to hear this from you, Mr. President. My team and our officers on the ground comprise only the most well-trained and patriotic individuals."

430.speaker: Lileas Graf
430.text: "With Bergia under complete control of the central administration, we will no longer hear reports of injustice against our Bludish citizens."

432.speaker: Lileas Graf
432.text: "Are you truly supportive of Governor Bron's policies, Mr. President?"

433.speaker: Lileas Graf
433.text: "So here's my offer. I'll work on the proposal for abolishing the Special Zone of Bergia."

434.speaker: Lileas Graf
434.text: "This would also mean abolishing the region's special governor position."

436.speaker: Player
436.text: "I don't want to move against a prominent USP figure who's protected by Mr. Hawker right now. I'm sure you understand."

437.speaker: Player
437.text: "No. But I don't want my administration to be involved in such a politically charged issue."

438.speaker: Lileas Graf
438.text: "But the reality is that we need to address the security problems in Bergia. This Bludish issue has the potential to get out of hand."

439.speaker: Player
439.text: "Yes. I think he's doing a good job."

440.speaker: Lileas Graf
440.text: "I thought the same at first. But it's clearly not working. The Governor is following his own independent policies, which is detrimental for the country as a whole."

441.speaker: Lileas Graf
441.text: "I see. I understand your concern, Mr. President."

442.speaker: Lileas Graf
442.text: "I would have agreed with you several years ago, Mr. President. But the policies of the governor are clearly not working."

443.speaker: Lileas Graf
443.text: "I want us to abolish the Special Zone and turn Bergia into a region like any other -- giving my security forces full authority over it."

447.speaker: Lileas Graf
447.text: "We just need to prepare a comprehensive plan and proposal for it."

448.speaker: Lileas Graf
448.text: "You can enact it with your emergency powers when it's ready, Mr. President."

456.speaker: Lileas Graf
456.text: "With Bergia under complete control of the central administration, we will no longer have failed operations or rogue governors to worry about."

457.speaker: Lileas Graf
457.text: "With Bergia under complete control of the central administration, we can efficiently enforce the emergency and bring stability to the region."

459.speaker: Player
459.text: "I am all for it, Lileas. I support this idea."

464.speaker: Lileas Graf
464.text: "We will hold local municipal elections just like every city in Sordland, and regional security will be under the full control of the Ministry of the Interior. We will no longer allow Bergia to have its own security force that defies orders from the central government."

465.speaker: Lileas Graf
465.text: "Regional security will be under the full control of the Ministry of the Interior. We will no longer allow Bergia to have its own security force that defies orders from the central government."

466.speaker: Lileas Graf
466.text: "And we will hold local municipal elections just like every other city in Sordland. Probably not before the emergency period ends, of course..."

467.speaker: Player
467.text: "All right. I will support you. Start working on it immediately."

468.speaker: Player
468.text: "No, I will not support this proposal, Ms. Graf. I'd rather keep the Special Zone as it is."

469.speaker: Lileas Graf
469.text: "I knew you would see reason, Mr. President."

470.speaker: Lileas Graf
470.text: "I will start working on the proposal immediately. It is very important to get this right, so it will take some time."

471.speaker: Lileas Graf
471.text: "My estimate is that it will be ready sometime after our midterm cabinet meeting."

472.speaker: Player
472.text: "Sounds good, Ms. Graf. I'm counting on you."

476.speaker: Narrator
476.text: She bid her farewell and left the room.

477.speaker: Lileas Graf
477.text: "Great. I'll get to work. See you later, Mr. President."

479.speaker: Lileas Graf
479.text: "I must say I'm disappointed, Mr. President."

483.speaker: Player
483.text: "I'm sorry to disappoint you, Lileas. But it is what it is."

484.speaker: Player
484.text: "Next time, don't come to me with excuses and problems, but with actual results. Please."
